summary: The exact navigational-scaffolding sentence the brief names as the recurring failure is still rendered in the /about/ hero deck. It tells the visitor what order to read the page in.
evidence: Rendered <main> line 4 of /about/: "One industry, since 1994, and nobody to answer to but the client. That's why Damian will hand your growers the outlook and the uncomfortable half of it in the same hour. Read the credentials first if you're the one signing the contract." Round 3 flagged the whole deck ("Below: the biography, the four credentials behind it, and the books. Read the credentials first if you're the one signing the contract."). Only the first half was removed; the instruction survived verbatim. `git grep 'Read the credentials first' HEAD -- app` returns nothing, so this string does not exist in the last commit: it was written by a fix. The round-4 fix pass identified it and explicitly declined to touch it ("NOT MINE, AND STILL LIVE") to avoid a collision, which means a half-removed sentence now reads as a completed fix and will ship. It is also the only sentence in the deck that is not about Damian.
suggestedFix: Delete the sentence. The deck's first two sentences already carry the whole claim and end on a strong beat ("the uncomfortable half of it in the same hour"). If a third sentence is wanted, it must be about the man or the offer, not about the page.

summary: A rendered cutline tells the visitor which copy on the page is verbatim and how complete the site's own attribution data is. This is a sourcing note, not copy.
evidence: Rendered <main> line 8 of /reviews/: "Every quote below is the sender's own wording. Nine of the ten came with a name attached." Both sentences are about the rebuild's editorial handling, not about Damian: the first is the verbatim-sourcing note the brief bans, the second exists only to pre-empt a reader noticing that one of the ten testimonials has no attribution line. Absent from HEAD (`git grep "sender's own wording" HEAD -- app` returns nothing), so a fix wrote it. A meeting planner assumes a testimonial is the sender's own wording; saying so out loud invites the opposite doubt.
suggestedFix: Cut both sentences. If the section needs a standfirst above the wall, write one about what the notes have in common (they arrived unprompted, after the event, from the person who signed the contract) rather than about how they were transcribed.

summary: The closing band panel added this round counts the page's own contents instead of stating a fact about the business, and restates the hero deck's arithmetic word for word.
evidence: Rendered <main> lines 56-62 of /reviews/: "ON THE RECORD / 14 / TESTIMONIALS ON THIS PAGE / Ten in writing, four on camera." The label is literally about the document. Every other route's closing panel carries a fact about the world: /contact-us/ "2,400+ AUDIENCES ADDRESSED", /join-the-conversation/ "40,000+ SUBSCRIBERS", /podcasts/ "40,000+ MONTHLY LISTENERS", /do-business-better-podcast/ "1994 / THE YEAR HE QUIT THE FORTUNE 500 JOB". It also duplicates the hero deck 500 words above it, which already reads "ten written notes ... plus four on camera. Fourteen out of 2,400+ audiences since 1994" (rendered line 4), so the page now states fourteen twice and the ten/four split twice. Absent from HEAD; the round-4 fix report documents adding it verbatim.
suggestedFix: Keep the panel (the band did need one) but make it carry a fact rather than an inventory. The repeat-booking claim this route is built on has no figure attached anywhere on the site, so the honest options are the site's existing 2,400+ / SINCE 1994 pair, or drop the value/label to something the hero does not already spend.

` with no trailing sentence, so a fix added it. /boasg/ also carries a second one at rendered line 29: "If you'd rather sample him before you join, the keynote program is one place and The Business of Agriculture podcast is another."

summary: Three routes explain the site's own lazy-loading implementation to the visitor, including a payload size in megabytes.
evidence: Rendered strings, all three visible in <main>: /the-business-of-agriculture/ line 30 "Libsyn's player brings about 2.5MB of its own code and artwork with it, so it waits here until you want it."; /blog-news/ line 57 "Nothing loads from YouTube until you press play." (app/blog-news/page.tsx:149); /blog/how-the-climate-crisis.../ line 16 "Nothing loads until you press play." (app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx:79). summary: The testimonial-count fact (ten written, four on video) is retold nine times in prose across four routes, three times within /speaking/ alone, and two of the retellings are the same sentence with the clauses swapped.
evidence: Measured paraphrase-insensitively over rendered <main>: /speaking/ x3 (eyebrow "TEN WRITTEN, FOUR ON VIDEO"; line 48 "Ten notes in writing and four on camera, sent by the people who signed the contract."; line 87 "Ten written notes and four video testimonials are on the testimonials page."), /reviews/ x4 (hero line 4; eyebrow "10 OF 2,400+"; heading line 39 "And what four of them said on camera"; panel line 62 "Ten in writing, four on camera."), /keynote/ x1 (line 89), /collaboration-opportunities/ x1 (line 109), plus two "READ THE TEN WRITTEN REVIEWS" CTA labels. It survived because there is no regex for it in scripts/dupe-check.mjs. The /keynote/ and /collaboration-opportunities/ versions are the defect shape the fix pass named on /contact-us/: "There's ten more on the reviews page, plus four on video." against "Ten more, plus four on video, are on the reviews page."
suggestedFix: Let /reviews/ own the arithmetic and spend it once there. On the three routes that only point at it, the link label already says "Read the ten written reviews", so the prose sentence can drop the counts entirely and say something the reader does not already have.

summary: The /about/ stat-ledger note asserts an unsourced claim about Damian's work rhythm that also contradicts the Home page's note on the identical four numbers.

summary: Both blog post routes fall below VOICE.md's contraction floor, which the guide defines as a rewrite condition rather than a note.
evidence: Measured over non-quote prose in rendered <main> (blockquotes, attributions, .dm-btn, .sr-only and .dm-faq stripped): post-eggflation 0.66 contractions per 100 words over 152 words, post-climate 0.74 over 136 words. VOICE.md section 8 check 3: "Under 1 per 100 words means the register is wrong", target 1.5 to 2.0. These are the only two routes on the site under the floor; the other 17 run 1.24 (/speaking/) to 3.61 (/join-the-conversation/), site aggregate 2.18 over 7,157 words. The copy is entirely rebuild-written, not parity: _source/pages/hello-world.md records JSON-LD wordCount 19 for the source post, so there is no verbatim body to preserve. Sample: "Simone Del Rosario wrote it for Straight Arrow News in December 2022, and Damian is quoted in it: producers were booking record profits while the grocery aisle turned into a meme."
suggestedFix: Add two or three contractions per post in the rebuild-written paragraphs (the standfirst and the closing booking band), which is enough to clear the floor on both without touching the quoted or attributed material.

summary: The /about/ hero deck still ends with a reading-order instruction: "Read the credentials first if you're the one signing the contract." This is the exact navigational-scaffolding class the brief names, and it is a live regression introduced by a Phase 6 fix.

That's why Damian will hand your growers the outlook and the uncomfortable half of it in the same hour. Read the credentials first if you're the one signing the contract." The round-4 fix pass flagged this itself as "NOT MINE, AND STILL LIVE" and declined to touch it; it has now shipped through a second round.

summary: The Libsyn player facade tells the visitor the site's own performance-engineering rationale, including a payload figure in megabytes: "Libsyn's player brings about 2.5MB of its own code and artwork with it, so it waits here until you want it."
evidence: app/the-business-of-agriculture/page.tsx:239-240, rendered inside <EmbedFacade> and confirmed in rendered <main> (line 19 of the stripped text, immediately above the "Load the player" button). It predates Phase 6 (present at HEAD), so it is an original defect three QA rounds missed rather than a fix regression, but it is the single clearest instance of the class on the site.

The deferral is invisible to a visitor who presses the button and should stay that way. Keep the engineering rationale in the code comment that already sits above it.

summary: A Phase 6 testimonial re-curation broke a factual claim: /keynote/ still says its three quotes are "from meeting planners who were in the room while it happened," but one of the three is now Brooks Breymeyer, whom no source identifies as a meeting planner or as having attended anything.

summary: The rebuild-written sentence "Meeting planners book Damian twice." still opens the copy on two different routes verbatim, with a third variant on Home.

summary: The /about/ hero deck still closes with a reading instruction, telling the visitor what order to read the page in. This is the exact recurring failure the brief names, it was flagged by the previous pass as still live, and it is still live.
evidence: Rendered at http://localhost:3100/about/, third line of <main>: "One industry, since 1994, and nobody to answer to but the client. That's why Damian will hand your growers the outlook and the uncomfortable half of it in the same hour. Read the credentials first if you're the one signing the contract." Source: app/about/page.tsx:176. Provenance: `git show HEAD:app/about/page.tsx` line 128 carries a clean, purely factual deck, deck="Purdue Ag Econ degree. Second City Chicago. An Indiana farm of his own. Since 1994 Damian has taken all three to 2,400 audiences in 50 states and 7 countries." A round-3 fix replaced that with the round-3 finding's own offending sentence ("Below: the biography, the four credentials behind it, and the books. Read the credentials first if you're the one signing the contract."), and the round-4 pass deleted only the first half. The surviving clause is navigational scaffolding: it names an on-page section and prescribes a reading order. It also duplicates work already done by the page: the credential bar is the very next thing after the hero, so a reader does not need to be told to get to it. The route's own meta description is clean ("Ag economist, comedian, and Indiana farm owner. Damian Mason has told Agriculture the truth about itself since 1994, with 2,400 audiences behind him."), which makes the deck the only place the instruction survives.
suggestedFix: Delete the third sentence. The two that precede it are already a complete, in-voice deck. If a third beat is wanted, make it about the man or the offer rather than about the page, e.g. a fact the hero does not yet carry (Purdue Ag Econ, Second City, the Indiana farm) rather than an instruction.

summary: The new closing-band panel on /reviews/ is labelled "Testimonials on this page", making it the only proof panel on the site that describes the website instead of describing the world.
evidence: Rendered at the foot of /reviews/: eyebrow "ON THE RECORD", value "14", label "TESTIMONIALS ON THIS PAGE", note "Ten in writing, four on camera." Source: app/reviews/page.tsx:228. Provenance: absent from HEAD (`git show HEAD:app/reviews/page.tsx | grep 'on this page'` returns only an unrelated code comment); the panel was added by the round-4 fix that filled the empty navy band. Compare every sibling panel, which I dumped across all 17 non-post routes: Home "THE BUSINESS OF AGRICULTURE / 70,000+ / VIEWS AND DOWNLOADS A MONTH"; /speaking/ "REPEAT BUSINESS / 2,400+ / AUDIENCES SINCE 1994"; /podcasts/ "THE REACH / 40,000+ / MONTHLY LISTENERS"; /meeting-coordinators/ "CALL THE OFFICE / 888.304.0702 / DIRECT LINE". Each of those counts something in Damian's career or gives the reader something to act on. "Testimonials on this page" counts the page's own contents, so the figure 14 proves only that somebody assembled fourteen items, not that fourteen clients vouched. A meeting planner does not care how many testimonials this page holds. The number and the note are both true and both already earned elsewhere on the route (hero deck "Fourteen out of 2,400+ audiences since 1994", section eyebrow "10 OF 2,400+", section No. 03 "FOUR VIDEOS"), so only the label is at fault.
suggestedFix: Relabel so the panel counts people rather than page furniture, e.g. "CLIENTS ON THE RECORD" or "MEETING PLANNERS WHO PUT IT IN WRITING". The eyebrow, the value 14 and the note "Ten in writing, four on camera." can all stand unchanged.

summary: A de-duplication fix left an unlinked "it's written up on the About page" pointer in prose, three lines above a real button that goes to exactly that page.
evidence: app/keynote/page.tsx:447-449 renders "He carries a Screen Actors Guild card, he has written a book about food and a book about business, and he hosts three podcasts between dates. If you want the long version, it's written up on the About page." The phrase "the About page" is plain text with no anchor. app/keynote/page.tsx:454-456, immediately below in the same block, is `<Button href="/about/" variant="secondary" size="lg">Read the full biography</Button>`. Provenance: `git show HEAD:app/keynote/page.tsx | grep 'About page'` returns nothing, so the sentence was added by the fix that moved the full bio onto /about/. The result is prose telling the reader where to go, with no affordance, sitting directly on top of the affordance that does the same job. Where the corresponding /about/ pointer would be needed it is the button that carries it.
suggestedFix: Cut the second sentence and let the button carry the wayfinding, or end the paragraph on a fact about Damian instead. If a prose link is genuinely wanted, it should be a link and the button should go.

summary: The /boasg/ bio paragraph now ends by inventorying another route's sections, which is the cross-route form of the exact construction the brief names as the recurring failure.
evidence: app/boasg/page.tsx:310-312 renders "{DAMIAN_BIO} The full biography, the credentials, and the books are <Link href=\"/about/\">on the About page</Link>." Rendered on /boasg/ section No. 02 as: "...On these calls that means the truth about Ag with no sugar coating on it. The full biography, the credentials, and the books are on the About page." Provenance: `git show HEAD:app/boasg/page.tsx | grep 'About page'` returns nothing. The `git diff HEAD` shows this arrived with the fix that cut the duplicated 78-word bio; the dedup rationale was correctly written into a code comment above DAMIAN_BIO, but the sentence itself made it into the rendered string. Structurally it is the same as the round-3 defect "Below: the biography, the four credentials behind it, and the books", just aimed at another route rather than at this one: it enumerates three of another page's section names. summary: The two paired Food Fear jackets collapse to postage stamps at 768 and 390, rendering at 44% of the single Do Business Better jacket beside them. The round-3 fix that collapsed the shelf to two cards names this exact failure in its own code comment and reports it as MEASURED AFTER at 768, but it is still what renders.
evidence: MEASURED, image bounding boxes on /about/: at 768 food-fear-book-cover 83x83 and food-fear-audiobook-cover 83x83 against do-business-better-book-cover 190x190 (2.29x). At 390: 146x146 and 146x146 against 315x240. At 1024: 198x198 vs 419x240. Only at 1440 do they reach parity (271x240 vs 566x240). Cause: app/about/page.module.css:127-141 sets .bookCover img { inline-size: 100%; block-size: auto; max-block-size: var(--size-jacket-h) }. In the two-up slot each jacket is a 1fr column, so at 768 the cover slot is 224px wide, minus 32px padding and a 24px gap leaves 84px per jacket. Width binds first and the 240px height cap never engages, so the comment's stated principle ("Height, not width, is what makes two jackets peers here") only holds at 1440. With object-fit: contain on a square-ish box the painted jacket art is roughly 44x62 at 768: the words FOOD FEAR are not readable and the audiobook edition the client supplied is not identifiable. Seen with my eyes in the 768 tile (round-4-mobile/02-about-768.png, fourth tile), where the pair read as two thumbnails beside a jacket 2.3x their size.
suggestedFix: Drive the pair from the block axis rather than the inline axis: give the two-up slot a fixed row height (block-size: var(--size-jacket-h)) with each img at block-size: 100%, inline-size: auto, object-fit: contain, and let the column widths follow the art. Then re-measure at 390, 768, 1024 and 1440 and require the paired jacket height to be within about 10% of the single jacket's on the same row at every width, not just at 1440.

summary: The .dm-section-close convention introduced in round 3 is not one convention in the rendered output.   /            128, 120, 128 (390) and 128, 120, 146 (768)

  /do-business-better-podcast/ 48
The shared rule at src/styles/sections-core.css:610 sets margin-block-start: var(--space-9) = 64px. Only /acres-tv/ (page.module.css:88) matches. On Home the element carries col-span-6 md:col-span-12 inside a dm-grid12, so the grid's own row-gap stacks on top of the 64px margin and doubles it. Seen with my eyes as a hole in round-4-mobile/01-home-390.png tiles 6 and 8 and round-4-mobile/01-home-768.png tiles 5 and 7: on Home No. 07 the pull quote and paragraph end and roughly 150px of nothing follows before the rule.
Same fix, second symptom: on /do-business-better-podcast/ the element also carries styles.stack (page.module.css:16-21, align-items: flex-start), which defeats the convention's own 390 branch (align-items: stretch). MEASURED: that CTA renders 270px wide at 390 where the identically-classed CTAs on Home, /speaking/, /keynote/ and /acres-tv/ all render 349px full-width. At 768 its rule spans 459px from x=278 instead of the container's 704 from x=32.
suggestedFix: Make the shared rule the only source of the spacing: delete the margin-block-start declarations from .actions in app/keynote/page.module.css and app/speaking/page.module.css and from .listFoot in app/do-business-better-podcast/page.module.css, drop align-items: flex-start from the .stack applied alongside .dm-section-close there, and on Home either take the element out of the grid flow or zero its margin so the grid row-gap alone provides the separation.
